The article discusses the mythical Hydra, a multi-headed serpentine creature from Greek mythology, and its possible origins in nature. Scientists have observed cases of polycephaly (having more than one head) in various animals, including two-headed fish, sharks, dolphins, and even domestic animals. This phenomenon is believed to be caused by genetic mutations or cellular displacements during embryonic development.

The article also mentions the SHH gene, which plays a significant role in determining the shape and composition of an organism's face, including the number of heads. Temperature is another factor that may influence the occurrence of polycephaly.

The Hydra's multiple heads and ability to regenerate could have been inspired by real-life animals with similar characteristics. Additionally, snakes grouping together during mating seasons might have also contributed to the creation of the Hydra myth.

Despite the low survival rate of two-headed organisms, they continue to fascinate humans due to their rarity and the psychological discomfort they evoke. The article concludes by suggesting that ancient authors may have been inspired by real-life polycephalic creatures when creating mythical monsters like the Hydra.

A head-on train collision occurred in Granges-pres-Marnand, western Switzerland on July 29, 2013, causing injuries to at least 44 people, including four seriously. One locomotive's driver is missing and search crews are attempting to access the crushed cab. Local police report that one person is still missing from the wreckage. This incident follows a high-speed derailment in Spain earlier this month that resulted in 79 fatalities.

Lego's sales increased significantly across Europe, America, and Asia compared to the same period last year. Notably, a new set featuring female scientists sold out on Lego's website within a weekend of its launch in early August.

The study published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition suggests that fast food is not the primary cause of childhood obesity but rather a symptom of poor dietary habits learned at home. Researchers from the University of North Carolina found that children who frequently eat fast food tend to have unhealthy diets regardless of whether they are eating at fast-food restaurants or not. The study, which analyzed data from over 4,000 children between 2 and 18 years old, categorized them as non-consumers, low consumers, or high consumers of fast food based on their calorie intake from fast-food establishments. The results showed that those who followed a Western dietary pattern when not dining at fast-food restaurants had the highest rates of being overweight or obese. The study suggests that public health efforts targeted at fast-food restaurants may be necessary but not sufficient to reduce child obesity if the remainder of the diet is not addressed. The researchers also found that a lack of adequate sleep, having parents with high body mass index (BMI), and having their eating habits restricted for weight control purposes are predictors of preschool obesity risk.

A study published in The Journal of Experimental Biology suggests that the Southeast Asian flying snake, Chrysopelea paradisi, adopts a flattened, UFO-like shape during gliding to optimize aerodynamic properties. This unique shape is not found in any other animal or engineered flyer. Researchers found that this shape is more effective than a cylindrical one for the snake's size and speed. The study also revealed that flying snakes undulate while gliding, but the reason behind this behavior remains a mystery. The team is now investigating why the snakes undulate during flight.

The House GOP's tax overhaul bill proposes to eliminate the adoption tax credit, which was created to help reduce financial barriers to adoption and subsidize costs for agency and attorney fees, travel, and post-adoption services. Adoption advocates have been fighting to make these credits refundable, as they believe it would particularly benefit lower and middle-class families who often don't reap the tax incentives of adoption due to the current nonrefundable nature of the credit. The elimination of the adoption tax credit could potentially lead to a chilling effect on adoption, according to adoption advocates. The credit was first championed by Republicans in 1994 as part of the "Contract With America" and was signed into law by President Bill Clinton in 1996.

On May 11, a team of 40 medical professionals at VCU Medical Center in Richmond, Virginia successfully delivered sextuplets (six babies) to Ajibola Taiwo, a native of Western Nigeria. The sextuplets, ranging from 1 pound, 10 ounces to 2 pounds, 15 ounces, are all doing well and receiving care in the Children’s Hospital of Richmond at VCU's neonatal intensive care unit. The Taiwos had been trying to conceive for 17 years and were initially overjoyed when they saw four heartbeats during their first ultrasound in November, only learning later that they were expecting sextuplets.

The delivery required extensive planning and coordination among various medical specialties, including maternal-fetal medicine, labor and delivery, nursing, anesthesia, respiratory, neonatal medicine, social work, nutrition, cardiology, and chaplain services. The team performed prenatal management and delivery planning, including pre-delivery drills and resuscitation exercises to prepare for the simultaneous arrival of six premature babies.

Kangaroo care, or skin-to-skin contact, has been provided to the sextuplets as soon as safely possible and as often as possible in the NICU to support attachment and bonding between the infants

Rose McGowan, a Harvey Weinstein accuser, is facing arrest after traces of narcotics were found in belongings left behind at Washington Dulles International Airport following a flight from Los Angeles earlier this year. Hillary Clinton surprised Katy Perry at a UNICEF event on Tuesday, presenting her with the Audrey Hepburn Humanitarian Award for her charitable efforts with the organization. Clinton praised Perry's compassion and activism, particularly her lyrics that encourage resilience in the face of adversity. Perry was moved to tears by the surprise appearance and thanked Clinton for inspiring her to use her voice for more than just music. The article discusses a controversial recommendation by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force that women in their 40s should not receive routine mammograms for early detection of breast cancer. Hearings are planned to discuss the recommendations further.

NBC News chairman Andrew Lack has reached a tentative agreement with Brian Williams that will keep him at the network after his six-month suspension ends in August. The details of Williams' new role are not yet known, but he is expected to have a reduced position on MSNBC and serve as a breaking news anchor for NBC News live special reports when Lester Holt, who has been filling in as the anchor of "Nightly News" during Williams' suspension, becomes the permanent anchor. In a speech at the Code Conference in California, Hillary Clinton attributed her loss in the 2016 presidential election to several factors, including suspected Russian cyberattacks, the Democratic National Committee's data operation, and a "very broad assumption" that she would win. Serena Williams accidentally shared her pregnancy announcement photo on Snapchat while she was on vacation. Tom Cruise and Katie Holmes' divorce has been finalized, marking the end of one of Hollywood's most high-profile marriages. Scientists have discovered that the larvae of the Argentine horned frog, known for their aggressive and carnivorous nature, emit a metallic-like sound when threatened. This is the first evidence of sound production by the larvae of anurans (frogs and toads). The discovery was made by Dr Guillermo Natale and his team from the National University of La Plata in Buenos Aires while studying the mating calls of adult frogs. The tadpoles produce the sound by pushing air out of their lungs, and it is believed that the distress call helps prevent cannibalism among the tadpoles. This finding suggests that other tadpoles may also communicate using sounds underwater. The Argentine horned frog tadpoles are difficult to find in the wild, so the researchers caught a wild pair of breeding adults and reared them in captivity to study the noise further.

Ron Paul's statement "We are all Austrians now" refers to a specific form of capitalism known as "Austrian economics," which is more libertarian and anarchic than mainstream forms. This school of thought, originating from Ludwig Von Mises and his student Murray Rothbard, rejects government intervention in the economy, including stabilization measures for macroeconomic fluctuations. They believe that stimulative policies cause recessions by producing unsustainable bubbles. However, critics argue that this theory doesn't explain recessions effectively and overlooks the role of expectations feedback in macroeconomic policy.

In the current economic context, Ron Paul's statement could be interpreted as a reflection of his belief in Austrian economics and its potential application in addressing the ongoing recovery process. The article suggests that the natural rate of interest, which determines equilibrium between savings and investment, has fallen below zero due to the financial crisis, making it difficult for the Federal Reserve to stimulate the economy further. However, as unemployment decreases and the economy recovers, the gap between the natural and actual interest rates will narrow, leading to economic growth and recovery.

The article predicts a recovery characterized by increased bank credit, growth in durable goods purchases, a return to normal levels of housing construction, and an end to public sector layoffs. This recovery is expected to be significant compared to the past four years but may not result in a tight labor market or rapidly rising wages

The U.S. Department of Labor has filed lawsuits against the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (FLDS) and some of its leaders, accusing them of using child labor during a 2012-13 pecan harvest without paying members for their work. The Department of Labor is seeking $1.9 million in penalties for child labor violations and back wages for the workers. Additionally, a construction company owned by an FLDS member has been accused of violating a 2007 court order regarding child labor laws.

The Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston has released a previously unseen surveillance video from 25 years ago, showing an unidentified man entering the museum through the same door as the thieves did 24 hours before the infamous art heist. Law enforcement officials are hoping that releasing this low-resolution footage will help identify the man or his vehicle and lead to the recovery of the stolen artwork, worth at least $500 million. The video shows a security guard admitting the man into the museum's reception area at about 12:49 a.m. on March 17, 1990, nearly exactly 24 hours before the heist. The man is also seen getting out of a car matching the general description of one reported to be parked outside the museum minutes before the theft. No one has ever been charged in the heist, and a $5 million reward has been offered by the museum for information that leads to the recovery of the stolen artwork in good condition.

The U.S. and China have imposed new sanctions against North Korea at the United Nations in response to its recent nuclear test. Meanwhile, IBM's Sequoia supercomputer has taken the top spot on the list of the world's fastest supercomputers, surpassing Japan's K Computer made by Fujitsu. The U.S. now leads the world in high performance computing, with IBM claiming five out of the top 10 spots on the list. Sequoia tested at 16.32 petaflop/s, consuming 7.9 megawatts compared to the K computer's 12.6 megawatts, making it more energy efficient. The first computer to take the top position on the list was the CM-5/1024 in 1993, designed by Thinking Machines. Sequoia is 273,930 times faster than the CM-5/1024.

The bigger challenge for YouTube is to get people watching longer, in order to compete for TV ad budgets.

The Parnell's mustached bat (Pteronotus parnellii) is a species native to North, South, and Central America with a range stretching from southern Sonora, Mexico to Brazil. Its lips are pointed upwards creating a funnel-shaped mouth, and it roosts in caves and tunnels, occasionally with other bat species.

The bat appears on the IUCN Red List with a conservation status of "Least Concern." Researchers have recently found that its brain has hemispheric specialization for sound processing similar to humans, with the left side better at processing fast sounds and the right side processing slow ones. This finding challenges the notion that only humans use different sides of their brains for sound processing and opens a pathway for studying bat brains to understand certain human language disorders and potentially improve computer speech recognition.

The study was supported by grants from the National Institute on Deafness and Communication Disorders and the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development. The researchers report having no personal financial interests related to the study.

In a study published in Scientific Reports, researchers from the University of Auckland and the University of Lincoln identified and isolated six major strains of Saccharomyces cerevisiae (a type of yeast) present at each of six New Zealand wine-producing regions. They then inoculated these 36 strains individually into sterilized Sauvignon Blanc grape juice to begin fermentation, controlling for all other factors. The resulting wines were tested for the presence and quantity of 39 volatile compounds and other quality parameters such as ethanol, acidity, and sugar.

The chemical signatures of the wines showed a large degree of overlap, but those produced by yeast strains from the same region tended to cluster, indicating that the wines did indeed exhibit a regional character. The most distinct regional signature belonged to those wines produced by yeast strains from Nelson, located at the northern end of New Zealand's South Island. These wines had particularly high concentrations of compounds that are known to impart apple and sweet fruit sensory effects.

The study provides the first quantitative demonstration of a microbial component of terroir, which is the distinctive regional conditions thought to shape a wine's character. The researchers suggest that further study is needed to determine whether other fungi and bacteria may also be contributing to regional wine characteristics.

There are no vaccines for this strain of enterovirus, so doctors advise good hygiene practices such as washing hands, staying up-to-date on vaccinations, and protecting against mosquitoes to prevent illness. AFM can cause long-term disabilities and there is currently no proven effective treatment.

This creates an intense trauma bond between the target and the abuser, making it difficult for the victim to leave the relationship. Children of narcissists are particularly vulnerable to love bombing due to their deep desire to be loved and validated, their history of triangulation, and their tendency to mistake superficial alliances for deep connections. To resist manipulative tactics, one should seek internal validation, pinpoint what makes them irreplaceable, differentiate between connection and flattery, and be selective about who they let into their life.

Researchers at the Georgia Institute of Technology have created a miniature replica of Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa that is significantly smaller than the original. By heating tiny spots on a plastic substrate, they triggered chemical reactions to produce variations in molecular concentrations, resulting in lighter or darker shades of gray. This technique could potentially be used for nano-manufacturing due to its ability to vary the surface concentration of molecules on such short length scales. The researchers believe that TCNL could enable a wide range of experiments and applications in various fields, including nanoelectronics, optoelectronics, and bioengineering.

The article from Bloomberg Businessweek reveals that retailer Target was alerted about a security breach on their systems nearly two weeks before they took action, despite having a $1.6 million malware detection tool from FireEye installed. The breach eventually compromised up to 40 million customers' credit card data, with personal information of 70 million customers potentially affected.

The report contradicts Target's previous statements about the incident, as they claimed to have only learned of the attack in mid-December. According to the article, Target's security team disabled an option that automatically deletes malware when it's detected, leading to the breach. Target's President and CEO Gregg Steinhafel has announced a company-wide probe to determine what happened, while the CIO during the hack, Beth Jacob, resigned earlier this month.

The article also speculates that the perpetrator of the hack may be Andrey Khodyrevskiy, a Ukrainian hacker known as Rescator, but there is no definitive proof linking him to the attack.

This delay will only affect new transgender recruits, not the estimated 15,500 already serving. The article discusses the ongoing controversy surrounding a fragment of papyrus known as the "Gospel of Jesus's Wife," which refers to Jesus as being married. First discovered in 2011, the fragment was introduced to the public by Harvard professor Karen L. King in 2012, causing widespread debate and skepticism about its authenticity.

Recent scientific tests have provided evidence supporting the document's authenticity. Carbon dating suggests that it dates back to the 8th century AD, while chemical composition analysis revealed ink consistent with that used by ancient Egyptians. Microscopic imaging showed no signs of modern ink pooling, which could indicate forgery.

However, some scholars still question the fragment's authenticity, arguing that it appears to be a pastiche of the Gospel of Thomas and contains grammatical errors that a native Coptic speaker would not make. Despite these criticisms, King maintains that the document is likely an authentic artifact from ancient times and offers insights into early Christian debates about the role of women, family, and celibacy in spiritual life.

The full findings will be published in the Harvard Theological Review on Thursday, March 10, 2023.

The bomb that exploded in Chelsea, New York City on Saturday was found to contain residue of an explosive compound called Tannerite. Tannerite is a binary explosive, which means it consists of two separate components - ammonium nitrate and aluminum powder - that are not explosive on their own but become so when mixed together. The compound is easy to find and can be purchased online or in stores. Tannerite is popular for target practice because it produces a loud bang and a puff of smoke when hit with a fast-moving bullet, making it more obvious when a target has been hit.

The ATF does not regulate the sale and distribution of Tannerite, even when sold together in binary "kits." However, mixing the binary components together constitutes manufacturing explosives, and the ATF advises that these products should be treated with caution and in accordance with manufacturer's instructions as they are high explosives.

Tannerite Sports is working to determine if their product was used in the Chelsea explosion, but the company has said that it can only be detonated by the impact of a high-velocity bullet, and there have been no reports that a gunshot was used to trigger the bomb. Some experts have suggested that Tannerite could potentially be used in a terrorist attack if improperly detonated, such as with a pressure cooker or old-fashioned flip phone.

In Texas, a final push was made by abortion rights advocates against proposed state rules that would require abortion providers to cremate or bury fetal remains. The Watergate parking garage in Arlington, VA, which played a crucial role in the Watergate scandal, is set to be demolished as part of a redevelopment project by Monday Properties. The company plans to replace two aging office buildings with a 32-story apartment or condo building and a 29-story office building, totaling nearly 1 million square feet of commercial and residential space.

The parking garage, built in the early 1960s, is nearing the end of its useful life and will be torn down during the redevelopment. However, Arlington County officials have erected a historical marker outside the garage that commemorates the spot where Washington Post reporter Bob Woodward met his source "Deep Throat" (later revealed to be FBI official Mark Felt).

Monday Properties plans to preserve the historical marker and incorporate it into their redevelopment, although it will likely be removed and stored during construction. The company appreciates the history of the site and aims to find an appropriate way to honor it in the new development.

The demolition and subsequent construction are expected to take place after Monday Properties receives county approval, but a specific timeline has not been announced yet. The Arlington County Site Plan Review Committee is scheduled to hold a meeting about the development proposal on October 21st.

A young Indian girl, believed to be between 10-12 years old, was found living with a group of monkeys in a forest in Uttar Pradesh, India. The girl was emaciated, unable to speak, and displayed "monkey-like" traits when she was first brought to a hospital. The Cleveland Police Department is facing reforms due to a federal investigation that found a pattern of excessive force by officers. Attorney General Eric Holder announced this on Thursday, stating that there is reasonable cause to believe the police department engages in a pattern and practice of using excessive force.

China has undergone significant economic reforms since the late 1970s, transitioning from a centrally planned system to a more market-oriented one. These reforms have led to a tenfold increase in GDP since 1978 and have made China a major global player. From 2013 to 2017, China had one of the fastest growing economies in the world, averaging slightly more than 7% real growth per year. China became the world's largest exporter in 2010 and the largest trading nation in 2013. However, China's per capita income is below the world average.

Austin Pledger's lawyer stated that this trial provided a public window into the real risks associated with the drug, as it is one of over 1,200 similar cases pending in Philadelphia courts.

A 12-year-old boy named Reginald Fields from Maple Heights, Ohio has seen a significant increase in his lawn care business, "Mr. Reggie’s Lawn Cutting Service," after a viral video showed him accidentally cutting a neighbor's grass while mowing a customer's yard. The incident prompted the neighbor to call the police, but no action was taken against Reginald. The video has resulted in an influx of requests for Reginald's services from people across the city who want to support his business. Reginald plans to use the money he earns this summer to buy new equipment and expand his business.

The discovery of a rock shelter in southern Australia's Flinders Ranges has revealed evidence of human settlement dating back 49,000 years. Archaeologist Giles Hamm made the chance find with aboriginal elder Clifford Coulthard during a survey of the area. The site, known as Warratyi, contains sophisticated tools and bone fragments from extinct megafauna, such as the Diprotodon optatum. Scientists have determined the age of the site at 49,000 years, pushing back the timeline for human settlement in Australia. The discovery challenges the consensus view that humans arrived 50,000 years ago and suggests they may have reached northern parts far earlier. The site also provides evidence of human interaction with megafauna, suggesting they hunted and consumed these animals. Excavation methods involved hand excavation within Warratyi rock shelter, using two trenches to uncover 4,300 objects and 200 bone fragments. Optical dating of quartz grains from the site supports the age determination. The discovery sheds new light on the early history of Aboriginal Australians, who are the oldest continued civilization in the world.

The suspect became agitated and pulled out a three-foot sword. Koba fell during the struggle and hit the man's legs with the golf club. The suspect dropped the cash register and escaped, but was later apprehended by police. Koba's son recovered the cash register. Police are still searching for the suspect and are asking for any information regarding his whereabouts.

A Florida police officer, Officer Laurie Graber, showed kindness and compassion by replacing an elderly woman's stolen engagement ring worth $400 from 1946. The victim, Betty Wagner, who has Alzheimer's, had worn the ring for 67 years until it was stolen from her hospital bed at Westside Regional Medical Center in Plantation, Florida. Officer Graber learned about the couple's story and purchased a replacement ring from J.C. Penney to comfort Betty and honor their long-lasting relationship. The original ring is still missing, but the new one has helped ease the pain for Betty and her husband, Arthur Wagner. Police are investigating the theft and have asked anyone with information to contact Broward County Crime Stoppers.

The discovery of the body was made on Tuesday, and an autopsy confirmed her identity, although the cause of death remains undisclosed. The discovery of a new strain of malaria, Plasmodium odocoilei, was made by accident during a study on mosquitoes at the Smithsonian's National Zoo. This parasite, which infects white-tailed deer, is the first-ever malaria parasite known to live in a deer species and the only native malaria parasite found in any mammal in North or South America. The study, led by Ellen Martinsen, suggests that the parasite infects up to 25% of white-tailed deer along the East Coast of the United States.

The discovery challenges the received understanding that "malaria wasn't supposed to be in mammals in the New World." The team's data shows that the two genetic lineages of the malaria parasites are substantially different from each other, suggesting that the deer malaria is native to the Americas and has been present for millions of years.

The researchers anticipate little danger to people from this newly discovered deer malaria but emphasize the importance of understanding the biology of other species as a foundation for both conservation and public health management. The study raises questions about whether the parasite might infect dairy cows or other hoofed species, and whether it could be causing low-level harm to white-tailed deer populations.

The study conducted by researchers at University College London suggests that the actual consumption of alcohol in England may be significantly higher than previously estimated due to underreporting by drinkers. The research found a significant shortfall between alcohol sales figures and self-reported consumption, indicating that as many as three-quarters of people may be drinking above the recommended daily alcohol limit. The study also found that total weekly consumption was higher than officially thought, with more men and women regularly exceeding the daily and weekly guidelines. The researchers plan to investigate the characteristics of those who underreport their alcohol consumption. They suggest that irregular drinking patterns, mixing drinks, and drinking at different venues may contribute to under-reporting. The study highlights the need for government drinking guidelines to reflect actual consumption instead of reported drinking, particularly when determining levels associated with harm. The Department of Health has stated that this will be taken into consideration in their alcohol consumption review.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has recommended expanding the screening process for all blood donations in the U.S. as a precaution against contaminating the blood supply with the mosquito-borne Zika virus. The FDA's updated guidance is due to the potential serious health consequences of Zika to pregnant women and children born to women exposed to the virus during pregnancy. The expansion of testing will be implemented gradually, with blood facilities in 11 states advised to begin testing within the next four weeks, and all states expected to comply within 12 weeks. There have been no cases of Zika related to blood transfusions in the U.S., but the FDA believes that expanded testing is necessary due to the potential for asymptomatic carriers of the virus. The FDA's acting chief scientist, Luciana Borio, stated that "as new scientific and epidemiological information regarding Zika virus has become available, it's clear that additional precautionary measures are necessary."

The international team of scientists has discovered a new species of centipede, named Geophilus hadesi, residing in the deep caves of Velebit Mountains in Croatia. This species is exceptionally rare as it spends its entire life cycle in caves, unlike most other geophilomorphs that only occasionally seek shelter there. The new species was named after Hades, the Greek god of the underworld, due to its deep cave dwelling habitat and unusual traits.

The Hades centipede is a carnivore that feeds on various invertebrate animals, equipped with powerful jaws bearing poison glands and long curved claws for grasping and holding onto prey. It dwells among an extraordinary number of pallid cavernicolous animals in the Velebit mountain range, which is a hot spot of subterranean diversity. The deepest record of this species comes from the Lukina jama - Trojama cave system, currently ranked as the 15th deepest cave in the world.

The discovery of Geophilus hadesi highlights the vast amount of unknown life forms that reside in caves and reinforces our limited understanding of these subterranean ecosystems. The research was published in the open-access journal ZooKeys.

The virus has been found in animal populations along coastal regions from Texas to the Chesapeake Bay, but until now, there hasn't been a way to test humans for it. The study published in Nature Communications reveals that a molecule called acetate, a product of fibre fermentation in the gut, may directly affect the hypothalamus, a part of the brain responsible for regulating appetite. This could explain how a high-fibre diet helps control weight by influencing the release of neurotransmitters associated with appetite control.

Researchers at Imperial College London fed mice fibre labelled with carbon-13 and found that acetate was not only present in the gut but also in the hypothalamus, where it was metabolized through the glutamine-glutamate cycle. The mice on a high-fibre diet ate less food and weighed less than control mice fed unfermentable fibre.

Although some experts question the interpretation of the results, the researchers believe that the same mechanism could be at work in humans. They are now planning to test their findings in people, with potential applications for new drugs to help control appetite and address issues related to weight gain. The study suggests that the modern diet, which contains less fibre than in Stone Age times, contributes to the current obesity epidemic.

Wind shear is typically measured as the difference in wind speed between 200 mb (the top of the troposphere) and a layer where a pressure of 850 mb is found, about 5,000 feet above the surface. This wind shear is computed over a large area, but smaller scale changes within the atmosphere may not be accounted for. Wind shear hurts tropical cyclones by removing heat and moisture they need, distorting their shape, and disrupting the delicate balance of inflowing low-level winds and outflowing upper-level winds that ventilate the storm.

He found that large vertical wind shears do not allow for area concentration of heat, making it difficult for tropical cyclones to develop in areas like the SW Atlantic and central Pacific where they do not occur. The U.S.'s strong economic and credit fundamentals, including its highly productive economy, exceptional financing flexibility, and low financial sector risks, continue to support its 'AAA' rating. However, public debt stabilization at elevated levels still makes the U.S. economy vulnerable to adverse shocks, and further deficit-reduction measures may be necessary in future years to contain government deficits and place public debt on a downward path over the medium to long term.

Researchers have discovered a large reservoir of melt water under the Greenland ice sheet, which could provide important insights into sea level rise. The discovery was made using a drill rig and ground-penetrating radar, and further research is planned to better understand the age and fate of the water in the aquifer.

2. Geoglyphs in Kazakhstan: Archaeologists have discovered over 50 geoglyphs in northern Kazakhstan, some shaped like swastikas. These structures were made from stone and are visible only from the air. Researchers believe they may have been built by a megalithic culture that also constructed elaborate stone monuments on a nearby island. The geoglyphs date back to the Neolithic and Eneolithic periods, making them older than Peru's Nazca Lines.

The article provides references for further reading on both topics.

The new study published in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B reveals that understory fires in the Amazon rainforest, previously hidden due to their location beneath the forest canopy, are causing significant damage to a larger area than deforestation for agricultural expansion. This was determined using a new satellite technique.

Understory fires burn slowly and unremarkably but can kill between 10-50% of trees in affected areas, making them an important source of carbon emissions that have not been adequately accounted for in climate models. The study found no correlation between understory fires and deforestation; instead, climate conditions, particularly low nighttime humidity, were identified as the most significant factor determining fire risk in the Amazon at a regional scale.

Researchers are currently investigating the climate mechanisms that make the southern Amazon more prone to burning, with soil moisture being a leading suspect. The study suggests that a severe fire season in the Amazon is often preceded by low water storage in the soil, which can be detected by satellites several months before the fire season.

This new understanding of understory fires could have implications for estimates of carbon emissions from disturbed forests.

The study highlights the profound impact that suicide can have on friends and family members, and emphasizes the importance of support for those affected by suicide loss. The researchers recommend offering practical help with day-to-day activities and encouraging open discussions about suicide to reduce stigma and promote mental health. The research, published in Nature, was conducted using infrared instruments on the Hershel Space Observatory. The study measured the deuterium ratio in Comet Hartley 2's water, which closely matches that of Earth's oceans. This finding challenges the assumption that asteroids were the primary source of Earth's water.

Comet Hartley 2 is unique because it originated from the Kuiper Belt, a region about 30 to 50 times further from the sun than Earth, while most other comets studied come from the Oort Cloud, which is much farther away. This difference in origin could explain why Comet Hartley 2's water composition differs from that of other comets previously analyzed.

The medical examiner's autopsy found no cause of death, but toxicology results will take two to three months.

Greenberg co-founded Grooveshark with Sam Tarantino in 2006 while they were both freshmen at the University of Florida. At its peak, the company had up to 40 million users a month and 145 employees. The service allowed users to upload songs and stream them to others, but it faced copyright infringement lawsuits from major record labels. In April 2023, Grooveshark settled with the industry and shut down operations.

Greenberg was widely regarded as a mentor to budding entrepreneurs and computer programmers in Gainesville. He helped establish programs like Grooveshark University, the Summer with the Sharks internship program, and the Founders Pad business incubator. Greenberg's death has been mourned by many in the tech community, who praised his contributions to the industry and his mentorship of others.

A man in Thailand, identified as Wuttisan Wongtalay, filmed himself killing his 11-month-old daughter on Facebook Live before taking his own life at an abandoned hotel in Phuket province. The incident occurred after an argument with his wife, and the video was removed by Facebook late Tuesday afternoon. The company has pledged to review its processes following a series of offensive broadcasts, including the shooting death of a man in Cleveland, Ohio, earlier this month. The Thai government has contacted Facebook regarding the removal of the videos, and YouTube also took down the video after being alerted by the BBC. The incident sparked anger on Thai social media, with relatives offering condolences to the family of the girl. This is not the first time Facebook Live has been used to broadcast violent content; previous incidents include a shooting in Chicago and a rape in Sweden that was live-streamed on the platform. Facebook is working to improve its review process for such content and is exploring the use of artificial intelligence to flag videos and photos that need to be reviewed.

Scientists have developed a stem cell therapy that can partially repair damage to the heart in monkeys. The treatment involves creating heart cells from donor skin cells and injecting them into damaged areas of the heart. While the treatment showed promising results, it also led to unusual heart rhythms in the recipients. More work is needed before human trials can take place. The therapy could potentially offer a new treatment option for heart attack survivors, as current long-term options are limited due to a shortage of donors for heart transplants. However, concerns remain about immune rejection and the integration of transplanted cells, which could result in irregular heartbeats.

Users posted status updates to clarify that they were not dead, and the incident was met with humor by technology reporters and Facebook users. Facebook later acknowledged this "terrible error" and apologized for the inconvenience. The memorial feature on Facebook, introduced in 2015, allows users to turn their account into a memorial page upon death or have it deleted after death.

The threat comes as reports suggest that North Korea may be preparing for another nuclear weapons explosion at its Punggye-ri test site.

However, if North Korea were to acquire an ample supply of fissile material and political pressures were to subside, it may soon conduct nuclear tests on an annual basis. This would have significant implications for current policy and the preparedness of allies.

He emphasized that stringent gun laws already exist in Colorado, and the issue is not with the laws but with individuals who are mentally disturbed. Romney signed a bipartisan assault weapons ban into law while serving as Massachusetts governor, which outlawed the type of rifle used in the Colorado shooting. Both presidential campaigns have toned down their rhetoric following the tragedy and are now engaging in a more thoughtful and serious debate.

The British Aerospace 146 jet suffered an electrical failure and was also affected by heavy rain during its final moments before disappearing from radar. The crash occurred as the team was en route to the Copa Sudamericana final against Atletico Nacional of Medellin.

However, unbeknownst to her, a pregnancy test was visible in the lower left corner of the picture. A man named David Weaver, aged 37 from Nelson, BC, skinny-dipped and swam with sharks at Ripley's Aquarium of Canada in downtown Toronto on October 12th. The incident occurred during a Friday Night Jazz event at the aquarium. Security escorted him out after he refused to leave, but he evaded them by slipping into a crowd of visitors. Weaver is also wanted for assaulting a man outside Medieval Times earlier in the same night. Police are searching for him and have identified him with help from the public. The aquarium is cooperating with authorities and is willing to press charges once Weaver is apprehended. No marine animals or patrons were injured during the incident, which was captured on video and has received over 5,000 views on YouTube.

Amy Winehouse, the troubled singer, died accidentally due to alcohol toxicity at her north London home in 2011. The second inquest confirmed the same verdict as the first one in October 2011, which had to be reopened due to irregularities in the first coroner's qualifications. Dr Shirley Radcliffe, the new coroner, recorded a verdict of death by misadventure at St Pancras Coroners Court.

On the day of her death, Winehouse was described as "her usual bubbly self" and there were no suspicious circumstances or evidence of illicit drugs in her system. However, the level of alcohol in her blood was over five times the drink-drive limit, and two empty vodka bottles were found on the floor of her bedroom.

The first coroner, Suzanne Greenaway, who oversaw the first inquest, was not properly qualified for the role. She had been appointed by her husband, Andrew Reid, who has since resigned from his position after disciplinary proceedings were launched against him. His wife also stepped down due to lack of experience.

None of Winehouse's family attended the second inquest as they were satisfied with the first one, which they said brought them some relief to finally know what had happened to Amy.

The incident occurred on Tuesday afternoon, leading to an evacuation of hotel guests and residents, as well as the closure of nearby streets for several hours. The victim lived on the third floor of the six-story landmark building, but it is unclear if she was affiliated with the club. Chaney had stopped to fuel up, but his card wouldn't work at the pump, causing him to go inside to pay. A pet pig named Dumplin in Indianapolis is being credited by police for potentially scaring away home intruders during a recent break-in. The homeowner, a single mother with four children, rescued Dumplin earlier this year and is relieved that the pig was not harmed during the crime. Unfortunately, burglaries are common in the neighborhood where the incident occurred. The homeowners hope that the suspects will be caught soon and encourage more people to consider adopting pet pigs. There's no word yet on if police have found the suspects.

The Miami Dolphins have terminated the employment of offensive line coach Jim Turner and head trainer Kevin O'Neill following an investigation into misconduct in the locker room. The investigation, led by Ted Wells, found that Turner tolerated and participated in harassment, lied to investigators, and attempted to convince a player to publicly defend another teammate. A new study by Pecan Street Research Institute suggests that solar panels facing west instead of south could produce more electricity during peak demand hours, contrary to conventional wisdom. The study, conducted on 50 homes in Austin, Texas, found that west-facing solar systems reduced the amount of electricity needed from the grid during summer peak demand by 65%, compared to a 54% reduction for south-facing panels. West-oriented panels are more effective at capturing solar energy late in the afternoon, when most people turn on their air conditioning and utility companies experience peak demand. The study has the potential to change the residential solar market, as it opens up the market to homeowners with west-facing roofs who previously thought they would not be good candidates for solar. However, more research is needed to determine the impact of this orientation during winter months.

The document summarizes the first year of Robert Mueller's investigation as Special Counsel into any links and/or coordination between the Russian government and individuals associated with President Donald Trump. Appointed in May 2017 following the firing of FBI Director James Comey, Mueller has remained tight-lipped about his activities except for indictments and plea deals.

In its first year, the investigation has obtained five guilty pleas and multiple indictments. Notable figures indicted include Paul Manafort, Rick Gates, George Papadopoulos, and Dutch lawyer Alex van der Zwaan. Mueller's team consists of 17 attorney staff members, with at least 12 registered Democrats and two unconfirmed members.

The investigation has faced criticism from Trump and his allies for alleged partisan bias, but both Justice Department policy and the Civil Service Reform Act prevent political affiliation from being considered when assembling Mueller's team.

Legal questions remain about whether presidents can be subpoenaed or indicted, and whether Trump can fire Mueller or use pardons to stymie the probe. The document discusses potential legal challenges in these areas but does not provide definitive answers.

A six-year-old autistic boy was found driving a miniature battery-powered ATV on the Bronx River Parkway in Mount Vernon, New York, on Sunday evening. The boy had initially gone missing from a city park and was later reported missing to the police by his family. Three good Samaritans slowed their vehicles to surround and protect the child from other traffic, eventually pulling him over to the side of the road. The boy was taken to Montefiore Mount Vernon Hospital for observation but was found to be okay. He has since been reunited with his family. The incident is currently under investigation.

A jaguar named Valerio escaped from its enclosure at the Audubon Zoo in New Orleans on July 14, 2018, resulting in the death of six animals: five alpacas, one emu, and one fox. Two more animals, an alpaca and a fox, died later due to their injuries, leaving only one fox as the lone survivor. The zoo was closed for a day following the incident but reopened on Sunday. The jaguar was captured and sedated by a vet team. No humans were harmed during the escape. The zoo acquired the alpacas in March from farms in Alabama and Mississippi, all of which were killed during Valerio's escape. The zoo has brought in grief counselors to support affected staff members. Visitors expressed concern about the incident and questioned the ethics of zoos. The jaguar exhibit was closed for repairs, and some enclosures were empty due to the loss of their inhabitants. A young girl named Lily left a heartfelt letter at the zoo in memory of the deceased animals.

China has announced a suspension of all coal imports from North Korea for the remainder of 2017, in line with United Nations Security Council sanctions imposed in November 2016. The ban aims to put pressure on North Korea to abandon its nuclear and ballistic missile programs. China is North Korea's largest trade partner and this suspension will significantly impact Pyongyang's foreign currency earnings as coal is North Korea's main export. The decision was made to comply with UN Security Council Resolution 2321, which imposed some of the toughest sanctions yet against North Korea following its disregard for an earlier UN ban on nuclear tests and missile launches. This move comes amid growing tensions on the Korean Peninsula following North Korea's latest ballistic missile test last week.

Retailers Walmart, Sears, and Amazon have removed a home decoration poster featuring a replica of the infamous Dachau concentration camp sign from their websites. The gate's German phrase "Arbeit macht frei," which translates to "work makes you free," was used by Nazis during World War II. The item was sold by third-party sellers on these marketplaces, not directly by the retailers themselves. Walmart and Sears have apologized for the oversight and removed the offending posters, while Amazon has yet to comment.

The incident sparked outrage on social media, with many finding it inappropriate to sell such a commemorative item as home decor. The sign was also found to be listed alongside other items, including ovens – a reference to the notorious use of ovens for cremating concentration camp prisoners at Dachau and elsewhere during World War II.

This incident highlights the delicate balance retailers must maintain when selling Nazi-related paraphernalia. In the past, eBay faced criticism for profiting from the trade in Holocaust memorabilia, leading to a refinement of its policies regarding the sale of potentially offensive items.

Overall, Kristof notes that it is difficult to gauge public opinion in an authoritarian country like Iran, but he believes that the demise of the current system is inevitable unless there is a war between Iran and the West. He suggests that such a conflict could provoke a nationalist backlash and potentially save the ayatollahs.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered emergency inspections of 175 Boeing 737 airliners, focusing on older models built in the 1980s and 1990s that have taken off and landed more than 30,000 times. The order comes after a Southwest Airlines jet suffered a tear in its roof during a flight on Friday. Inspections will be conducted using electro-magnetic technology to detect cracks invisible to the naked eye. The incident has raised concerns about aging aircraft safety and could lead to broader requirements for costly inspections. Southwest Airlines, which operates 78 of the affected jets, has already grounded several planes due to fatigue cracks discovered during inspections. The FAA is also investigating the cause of the tear in the Southwest jet's roof and has found additional cracks on the same seam where it ripped open.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit against North Carolina, alleging that the state's new voter ID law violates the Voting Rights Act by discriminating against African-Americans. Attorney General Eric Holder announced the lawsuit at Justice Department headquarters, stating that the law was intentionally designed to disproportionately exclude minority voters and contract the electorate.

The lawsuit objects to several key provisions of the North Carolina law, including the elimination of seven days of early voting, the end to same-day voter registration during the early voting period, and the end to the option of provisional ballots for voters who show up at the wrong polling place. The suit also challenges the photo ID requirement, as it disproportionately affects African-American voters and lacks evidence of widespread voter fraud.

The Justice Department is seeking to bar North Carolina from enforcing the new voter-ID law and to place the state under a requirement to have all changes to voting laws, procedures, and polling places "precleared" by either the Justice Department or a federal court. The department moved in July to put Texas under preclearance requirements following similar cases over redistricting and voter ID laws.

Critics argue that the law will disenfranchise African-American and elderly voters, while supporters claim it is necessary to protect the state's voters from potential fraud

The video, which was shot in May northeast of Edmonton, shows Josh Bowmar, a personal trainer and former competitive javelin thrower, hitting the bear with a hand-thrown spear. The Alberta government has announced plans to ban spear hunting this fall, and fish and wildlife officers are investigating the incident to see if charges are warranted under existing laws. Conservation groups have been pressuring for change, as they believe that spear hunting is inhumane due to the risk of an injured animal running off and suffering for an extended period. The video has received widespread criticism from both hunters and non-hunters, with many denouncing the kill as "barbaric" and "unnecessary."

It is not recommended to buy a Galaxy Note 7, even if one can still be found for sale.

Aspiring comedians are encouraged to pursue this major, but stand-up comics need experience in addition to education. It also helped create a sense of cohesion and group identification among Latter-day Saints, who saw themselves as a "peculiar people."

The practice of plural marriage was controversial and violated cultural and legal norms, leading to persecution and revilement. Despite these hardships, it benefited the Church in numerous ways, with many descendants being faithful Latter-day Saints who have been righteous parents, loyal disciples of Jesus Christ, devoted Church members, and good citizens.

Kim Kardashian is facing criticism from PETA for posting a video of herself riding captive dolphins on social media. The animal rights organization claims that swimming with dolphins held in captivity is intrusive, dangerous, and stressful for the animals. They argue that dolphins are denied their natural behavior and live in small tanks, which can lead to physical and psychological problems. Kardashian has been criticized before for her seemingly animal-unfriendly choices, such as sporting python boots and swimming with a giant sea lion. PETA also notes that aquariums and marine-mammal theme parks like SeaWorld are part of a billion-dollar industry built on the suffering of intelligent, social beings who are denied everything natural to them. The organization encourages people not to visit marine parks or zoos that keep ocean animals in captivity and to support legislation that prohibits the capture or restricts the display of marine mammals.

Nike has announced the release of their self-lacing shoe, the HyperAdapt 1.0, which brings to life the dream first depicted in Back to the Future II. The shoes feature an automatic lacing system that tightens when you step in and can be manually adjusted with buttons on either side. Nike previously created real-life versions of the self-lacing Air Mag sneakers from Back to the Future, but these were not intended for mass market. The HyperAdapt 1.0 will be available this year, exclusively for members of Nike+, during the holiday season in three colors. The technology used in the HyperAdapt 1.0 is similar to that used in the commemorative Air Mags, and Nike hints at future versions of the technology that could automatically adjust the fit based on biometric data.

David Steele, a 42-year-old veteran race car driver and multiple United States Auto Club national champion, was killed in a sprint car race at Desoto Speedway on Saturday night. Steele, who won several sprint car series championships and competed in some IndyCar and NASCAR races, was seeking his 100th career sprint car victory in Florida at the time of the accident. The incident occurred during the Southern Sprint Car Shootout Series race at the 3/8-mile asphalt track on State Road 64 East in east Bradenton. Steele's death brought stunned reactions across social media, with fellow drivers and racing teams expressing their condolences. The racing related fatality is the first at the speedway in many years. Steele is survived by his wife, Lynn Bunn Steele, and three young children.

The NSA's facial recognition program is separate from its bulk metadata collection program but requires court approval to collect images from American citizens. The agency has turned to new software to process the flood of images being included in digital communication, including social media, email, messaging, videoconferencing, and other types of online communications.

The NSA also relies on commercially available facial recognition technology like PittPatt, owned by Google, to process the data it is harvesting. Facial images, fingerprints, and other identifiers are now considered just as important to the NSA as written and oral communications. On September 9, 2015, Queen Elizabeth II will surpass Queen Victoria as Britain's longest-reigning monarch, having reigned for 63 years and seven months. The Queen thanked well-wishers for their messages of kindness and expressed that the title was not one she had aspired to. In Scotland, she formally opened the new Scottish Borders Railway and was praised by Scotland's First Minister Nicola Sturgeon for her dedication, wisdom, and exemplary sense of public service. In London, a flotilla of vessels took part in a procession along the Thames, and MPs paid tribute to the Queen in the Commons. The Queen will mark the moment privately with her husband, Prince Philip. Buckingham Palace released official photographs to commemorate the occasion, taken by Mary McCartney in the Queen's private audience room. The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge are expected to have dinner with the Queen at Balmoral later. The Queen is Head of the Commonwealth and sovereign of 15 Commonwealth realms in addition to the UK. Anti-monarchist group Republic called for reform, stating that the Queen's long reign was a reason for change, not celebration.

Patton Oswalt, a 48-year-old actor and comedian, married Meredith Salenger on November 4, 2017, at the Jim Henson Company lot in Los Angeles. The couple announced their engagement via Instagram in July, and Salenger shared pictures of their wedding ceremony on Sunday. Oswalt's first wife, Michelle McNamara, died unexpectedly in April 2016, and Oswalt didn't remove his wedding ring until a year after her passing. The couple's engagement came 15 months after McNamara's death, and they faced criticism on social media for moving on so quickly. However, both Oswalt and Salenger defended their relationship and expressed gratitude for finding love again.

John Caltabiano, a 49-year-old man from Catskill, New York, was sentenced to nearly five years in prison for disability fraud after being found guilty of conspiracy to commit mail fraud, five counts of mail fraud, and theft of government property. Caltabiano claimed he was blind due to a workplace accident in 2006 and collected over $1 million in benefits before being caught on camera driving, shopping, and going to the gym. His girlfriend, Colleen McCarten, was also found guilty of fraudulently obtaining federal and state disability benefits and received three years' probation. The investigation into Caltabiano's case was conducted by the Social Security Administration Office of the Inspector General and the Office of the New York State Workers' Compensation Fraud Inspector General. This case highlights the issue of disability fraud, which is a significant problem across the United States, with over 7,000 cases opened each year of suspected Americans trying to dupe the system.

The Costa Concordia fuel removal operation has commenced, nearly a month after the cruise ship ran aground off Tuscany. After delays due to rough seas and bad weather, pumping started on the first of 15 tanks believed to hold around 84% of the fuel on board. The process involves fixing valves on underwater fuel tanks and warming the oil to make it less gooey before extraction. Dutch shipwreck salvage firm Smit is overseeing the operation, which is expected to take 28 consecutive days to empty the tanks.

The Concordia incident has caused concerns about potential fuel leaks and contamination of the pristine waters off Giglio island, a protected sanctuary for dolphins, whales, and porpoises. However, there have been no reports of serious leaks so far. The ship capsized after the captain deviated from the planned course, causing delays in sounding the evacuation alarm. About 4,200 passengers and crew escaped, but 17 bodies have been found, and another 15 people remain missing and presumed dead.

A strong radio signal has been detected from the direction of HD164595, a sun-like star located approximately 95 light years away in the constellation Hercules. The signal was initially detected by the Russian Academy of Science's RATAN-600 radio telescope and is being considered as a potential candidate for an intelligent, extraterrestrial source. If confirmed, the signal could indicate the presence of a highly advanced civilization, capable of harnessing energy on a scale comparable to their host star (Kardashev Type II) or tapping into all the starlight that falls on their home planet (Kardashev Type I). However, it is also possible that the signal could be due to terrestrial interference. The SETI Institute and other observatories are currently attempting to confirm the detection and further study the signal's characteristics.

Amy Adams, a five-time Academy Award nominee, demonstrated her class and kindness by giving up her first-class seat on a Delta flight from Detroit to Los Angeles to an American serviceman. Jemele Hill, co-host of ESPN's Numbers Never Lie, shared the news on Twitter and spoke with TODAY.com via email about the incident. Adams reportedly noticed the soldier while waiting to board and later vacated her seat for him. Passenger Ernest Owens was able to take a selfie with Adams after the flight, and she explained that she had always wanted to do something like this. The serviceman was unaware of Adams' identity during the flight, but Adams stated that she did it to draw attention to the troops. Adams received her latest Oscar nomination last year for her role in "American Hustle." This act of kindness by Adams has been praised on Twitter, and Hill's show, Numbers Never Lie, airs weekdays at noon on ESPN2.

A ceasefire brokered by the United States and Russia has begun in Syria amid mixed messages from various rebel factions but with verbal backing from President Bashar Assad's government. The truce, which began at sunset on September 12, 2016, allows the Syrian government to continue striking Islamic State group and al-Qaida-linked militants for another week before the US and Russia take over the task. The deal was struck after months of talks between Russia and the US and requires both sides to allow unhindered access for humanitarian aid to besieged areas. If the truce holds for seven days, the US and Russia will carry out coordinated air strikes on militant groups. Rebel factions have expressed deep reservations about the deal. The Syrian army says it is implementing the truce, but rebel groups have been more guarded.

Chambers' father stated that she had never mentioned Tellis's name to the family. There is a possibility that prosecutors will choose to retry the case for a third time, but no decision has been made yet.

In addition to facing charges in Chambers' murder, Tellis will also be sent back to Louisiana to face charges in another homicide case there involving the murder of a student at the University of Louisiana Monroe in 2016. The NFL and Pepsi have responded by stating they have not yet extended a formal offer to any artist for the show, which will take place at Houston’s NRG Stadium on February 5, 2017. Former US President Barack Obama, in a rare interview since stepping down in January, expressed concern about the irresponsible use of social media, stating that it distorts people's understanding of complex issues and spreads misinformation. He suggested that leaders should find ways to create a common space on the internet that allows for diverse views without leading to societal fragmentation. Obama also discussed his time in office, citing Obamacare as a major achievement, and expressed optimism about the future despite global issues. The interview also touched on topics such as mental health, youth crime, climate change, and Prince Harry's upcoming wedding to American actress Meghan Markle.

The USS John S. McCain collided with an oil tanker near Singapore on August 21st, resulting in significant damage to the warship's hull and causing extensive flooding. Ten sailors are missing and four were hospitalized after being evacuated by helicopter. The Navy has ordered a thorough investigation into the incident, including a review of the possibility of "cyber intrusion or sabotage." Adm. Phil Davidson, head of the Navy's Fleet Forces, will lead the investigation. This is the second deadly mishap involving a U.S. Navy destroyer in the Pacific in the past three months, following the collision of the USS Fitzgerald off the coast of Japan in June. The Navy has also called for a review of the 7th Fleet's maintenance, personnel and equipment in the region, as well as a focus on surface warfare training. Some experts have speculated that GPS sabotage may have played a role in the collision, but it is unlikely due to the wide range of ships that would have been affected by such an attack. The investigation into the USS McCain collision is ongoing.

The panel wields no power to compel change from Ireland, but human rights watchdog Amnesty International said the findings should shame Ireland into further action. The Rich Earth Institute in Brattleboro, Vermont is investigating the use of human urine as a replacement for chemical fertilizers in agriculture. The institute collects urine from volunteers and processes it to remove pathogens before using it as a fertilizer. Urine contains essential plant nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which are usually mined or synthesized for agricultural use. By collecting and using human urine, the institute aims to divert these chemicals from waterways and reduce their environmental impact.

The project has been successful in increasing crop productivity, with trials showing that urine-treated fields were twice as productive as unfertilized controls. The institute has received funding from the USDA and is expanding its trials to three farms this year. However, public perception of the project remains a hurdle, with concerns about the "ick factor" and potential health risks.

The institute has developed strategies for eliminating pathogens in urine, such as solar pasteurization and long-term storage in warm greenhouses. They are also conducting studies on traces of pharmaceuticals in urine with the help of universities. The institute's founder, Kim Nace, uses a urine-diverting toilet at her home and welcomes visitors to learn about the project.

Twin car bomb explosions occurred in Damascus, Syria's capital, on Saturday, resulting in at least 27 deaths and nearly 100 injuries. The attacks targeted intelligence and security buildings, including a customs office and air force intelligence. The Syrian government blamed "terrorists" for the bombings, while no group has claimed responsibility. The opposition has accused the government of orchestrating the attacks to tarnish their image. The explosions come two days after the one-year anniversary of the uprising against President Bashar al-Assad and have been condemned by international leaders. Allegations of al-Qaeda involvement in the bombings have raised concerns about the Sunni-led uprising affecting minority populations in Syria.

Facebook is blocking any links or mentions of the social media website Tsu.co on its platforms, including Messenger and Instagram. This action was taken due to claims that Tsu links are spam, which Facebook defines as "sending bulk messages, excessively posting links ... and sending friend requests to people you don't know personally." The block has affected millions of posts and caused frustration among users, particularly those who use social media for professional purposes like photography or modeling.

In an Instagram post, Hart expressed his determination to fight this toughest battle yet, drawing on his past experiences as a survivor of numerous hardships. Additionally, he claimed the WWE U.S. heavyweight title on five separate occasions. Tragically, Hart's brother Owen died in 1999 after an accident during a performance at Kemper Arena in Kansas City, Missouri.

The article highlights a new report that reveals improper use of contact lenses, such as sleeping with them or using the same pair for too long, is causing serious eye injuries in many Americans. The report, published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), analyzed over 1,000 cases of contact lens-related eye infections reported to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration between 2005 and 2015.

Nearly one in five patients experienced significant eye damage due to these infections, including scarred corneas, the need for corneal transplants, or other types of eye damage. More than 10 percent of the patients required hospitalization or urgent care treatment. The report emphasizes that proper contact lens care is crucial to maintaining good eye health and preventing infections.

The CDC recommends annual eye exams, buying contact lenses from trusted sources, following proper cleaning and rinsing procedures, not sharing contacts, avoiding tap water for lens care, keeping the lens case clean, and never sleeping in contacts unless specifically approved by an optometrist. United's bug bounty program allows researchers to report potential security issues on their websites, apps, and online portals, with a maximum payout of 1 million miles for remote-code execution bugs.

Wiens plans to use the miles for coach class trips for his family, but may also splurge on a premium cabin trip. He found the vulnerability after poking through United's online systems for about six hours and was surprised by the large payout as he initially thought it would be worth fewer miles. Wiens is boasting that he earned 1 million airline miles without ever leaving the ground.
